references.text: The Sheep Gate (probatikē) in Jerusalem is mentioned in [ref:Neh 3:1|Nehemiah 3:1], where the high priest Eliashib and his brothers rebuild the Sheep Gate. This is the same gate that John refers to with the phrase "at the Sheep Gate" (epi tē probatikē).
[ref:Neh 3:32|Nehemiah 3:32] mentions the Sheep Gate as a reference point in the description of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall, confirming its location within the city.

[ref:Neh 12:39|Nehemiah 12:39] mentions the Sheep Gate in connection with the dedication procession along Jerusalem's wall, further confirming that this was a well-known gate in the city that John's readers would have recognized.

The Pool of Siloam in [ref:Joh 9:7|John 9:7] is another pool (kolumbēthra) in Jerusalem where Jesus performs a healing. John also explains there the meaning of the Hebrew name, reflecting his approach in 5:2.

The place called "Stone Pavement" (Gabbata) in [ref:Joh 19:13|John 19:13] is another example of John using Hebrew/Aramaic place names with explanations, just as he states here that the pool "is called Bethesda in Hebrew" (Hebraïsti Bēthesda).

[ref:Jes 8:6|Isaiah 8:6] mentions the waters of Siloam in Jerusalem and points to the theological and historical significance of water installations in the city—a background for the pools John mentions in his gospel.
